stops.name: Mirador Lago Sarmiento
stops.blurb: A huge lake that shades from turquoise to deep blue, with the whole Paine massif behind it. Look for the white thrombolite (living rock) formations along the shore.

stops.name: Laguna Amarga
stops.blurb: A salty lagoon by the main entrance gate, with the classic postcard view of the three Torres reflected in it. Flamingos are sometimes here.

stops.name: Laguna Azul
stops.blurb: A quiet, windswept lake reached by a gravel road, with a head-on view of the Torres from the north. Guanacos graze all along the drive.

stops.name: Mirador Nordenskjöld
stops.blurb: A roadside pull-out above milky-turquoise Lago Nordenskjöld, looking straight across at the Cuernos.

stops.name: Salto Grande
stops.blurb: A short, thundering waterfall where Lago Nordenskjöld drains into Lago Pehoé. It’s the first stop on the Mirador Cuernos walk.

stops.name: Mirador Lago Pehoé
stops.blurb: Lago Pehoé’s intense turquoise water with the hotel’s island, and the full Paine massif lined up behind it. Best in the late afternoon.

stops.name: Lago Grey & Glaciar Grey
stops.blurb: Blue icebergs from Glaciar Grey drift onto a grey-sand beach, with the glacier on the far shore. Reached by a suspension bridge and a beach walk.

stops.name: Mirador Río Serrano
stops.blurb: A broad river valley lookout near the southern park exit, with a last long view back at the massif.

stops.name: Mirador Lago del Toro
stops.blurb: The park’s largest lake, stretching south toward the Serrano valley. A good leg-stretch on the drive out.

stops.name: Laguna Sofía
stops.blurb: A calm lake under limestone cliffs, popular with climbers and condors, just off the road near the Cueva del Milodón. A good last stop before the airport.
